metadata.title: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [Januar 1942], SZ-AAL/B1.192

## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [Januar 1942], SZ-AAL/B1.192
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.192
- Datum: 01.1942
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 3 Scans

pages.transcription:
Dear Hannah & Manfred, in our monotonous and quiet existence was today
a little excitement; our gardener's wife {she is all day in a factory} who lives in the little hut behind our
bungalow got a child today and Manfred would have had something to learn -
how primitive the thing happens here which is quite complicated in our world. In
a little room, half of my study {in Petropolis} were during the great moment the husband, the
midwife, a sister, her child, a dog so that was no room at all; every even the
smallest comfort like running water is missing in this small space which has still
the kitchen-shore in it and nevertheless a brown boy was brought to the world, a
very quiet child, which makes no noise till now. Lotte was very excited about
not so the husband who immediately after went quietly to the café. One is al-
ways astonished by the poverty of the people here and one learns how many things
of our life are superfluous - if I remember Rene Fülöp's dies with all kind
of sterilisations and protections; here a black midwife does (not very cleanly)
all the work and the children grow nevertheless here like strawberries - our
black maid has no less than five. Living here means to get knowledge of
life, all is here (except in the Frischauer luxurious quarters) like two hun-
dred years ago and this gives here life a great charm; people live the old
family life and are happy to have a dozen children without to worry how to
feed them and God helps. It would be strange for us to return to European
and Northamerican ideas after all this experiences - The one big advantage
is that one is not more so afraid to become poor. In such countries one could
live with very few if one would forget his former standard. We had not very
good weather here, since 40 years it did not rain so much in Brazil but
we make every good moment our long walks (mostly with our dog) and dis-
cover always new picturesq sceneries; at night there are myriads of glow-worms
the whole forest glittering like a christmas-tree. Altogether we are very happy
to be here instead of Northamerica and Lotte feels somewhat better - I am
not yet satisfied completely, but I hope that she will stop soon her night-music
especially as summer is now beginning. I have not worked too much -
depressed by the eternity of war, the daily rain, but I hope now to start
as it is senseless to wait for better times one two three years. From Era
we have very good news and our confidence in Mr. Schaeffer is like before
very great - I believe it was thousand times better that Eva has grown
up with children of all ages, kinds, religious, languages and was obliged
to do many things herself as to remain always at home as the only child
- I envy you the moment when you will have her again. I hope you have
a fairly good time and my matters give not too much annoyance to you -
I myself have written everything I had in the "Raumfang" and cannot understand
the people who believe that life will continue after the war on the same old and standard of
September 1939. We hope to get soon good news from you. Heartest regards and love to all Stefan
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief von Stefan Zweig. Die Randnotiz am linken Rand wurde in den Textfluss integriert, da sie den Satzbau ergänzt.
